name: King of the Foulweald

meta.previous: Between a Rock and a Thistlefur

summary: Karang Amakkar orders a Horde strike against the Foulweald furbolgs southeast of Astranaar. Horde champions plant a war banner on the tribe’s sacred totem mound, drawing out Chief Murgut and killing him.

sections.title: A Show of Force
sections.body: Karang Amakkar at Zoram'gar Outpost sees the corrupted Foulweald as a danger to the Horde. The tribe is smaller than the northern Thistlefur, but its members are fierce. Rather than wait for them to ambush Horde patrols, Karang orders a show of force meant to break their will.

sections.title: Desecration and Challenge
sections.body: Greenpaw Village lies northeast of Mystral Lake. Karang prepares a tribal war banner to plant in the center of the Foulweald totem mound, insulting the tribe’s ancestral spirits and pride. Furbolg defenders rush to tear it down, and Chief Murgut emerges to defend his honor in open combat. Taking Murgut’s personal totem breaks the tribe’s leadership and establishes Horde supremacy in the area.

faq.q: Who orders the death of Chief Murgut?
aliases: quest giver king of the foulweald
who gives king of the foulweald
faq.answer: Karang Amakkar, an orc at Zoram'gar Outpost on Ashenvale’s western coast, orders Chief Murgut’s death after investigating the neighboring Thistlefur furbolgs.
Greenpaw Village lies southeast of Astranaar, northeast of Mystral Lake, and just south of Ashenvale’s main eastern highway.

faq.q: Why does the Horde plant a banner on the totem mound?
faq.answer: Karang’s banner is planted on the sacred totem mound to provoke the Foulweald. The insult drives them to attack and brings Chief Murgut into open combat to defend his standing.
The Foulweald are one of Ashenvale’s furbolg tribes, driven mad and corrupted after the Third War. Though fewer in number than the Thistlefur, they remain violent and hostile to outsiders.

faq.q: What does retrieving Murgut's Totem accomplish?
faq.answer: Taking Chief Murgut’s totem to Zoram'gar Outpost proves his defeat. Without their leader and with their sacred mound disgraced, the surviving Foulweald are intimidated into avoiding further conflict with the Horde.

faq.q: How does this quest fit into the earlier furbolg investigations?
aliases: between a rock and a thistlefur connection
faq.answer: Karang turns south to the Foulweald after dealing with the northern Thistlefur in 'Between a Rock and a Thistlefur.' He seeks to crush them before they can launch coordinated raids.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you see Karang Amakkar use shows of force to cow hostile Ashenvale tribes and secure central trails for Horde supply caravans.
As an orc, you know that provoking an enemy chieftain into single combat is a classic way of war, favoring strength and decisive confrontation over long skirmishes.
As a shaman, you recognize the Foulweald’s distorted totems and aggression as signs of the spiritual imbalance that plagued Ashenvale’s native tribes after the Burning Legion’s invasion.
